back: $(H,n)$, $(H,H)$, $(H)$, $(H)$ (batched $(B,H)$). Row-batch code: `X_t @ Wxh.T + h @ Whh.T + b`.

front: What does unrolling an RNN give?
back: A feed-forward network of depth $T$ whose layers share the same weights; train it with ordinary backprop (BPTT).
$\bar a_t=\bar h_t\odot(1-h_t^2)$; $\bar h_{t-1}=W_{hh}^\top\bar a_t$; $\bar W_{hh}\mathrel{+}=\bar a_th_{t-1}^\top$; $\bar W_{xh}\mathrel{+}=\bar a_tx_t^\top$; $\bar b\mathrel{+}=\bar a_t$.

front: Why are RNN weight gradients sums over time?
back: The weights are shared by all steps; the chain rule adds the contribution of each copy.

front: What must the forward pass cache for BPTT?
back: Every hidden state $h_t$ (and the inputs). Memory grows linearly with $T$.
Classification/regression: loss on the last state only. Annotation (tagging): a classifier and loss at every step, summed.
$\lVert\partial h_T/\partial h_0\rVert\le\lVert W_{hh}\rVert^T$ because $0<1-h^2\le1$; if $\lVert W_{hh}\rVert<1$ the gradient decays geometrically.
In the linear regime $\lVert W_{hh}^T\rVert\approx c\,\rho^T$: vanishes for $\rho<1$, explodes for $\rho>1$, knife edge at 1.

front: Why can tanh turn an explosion into vanishing?
back: Large states saturate ($h\to\pm1$), so $1-h^2\to0$ and the Jacobian shrinks.
$g\leftarrow g\min(1,\tau/\lVert g\rVert)$ with $\lVert g\rVert$ over all parameters; same direction, bounded step. Fixes explosions only.
Backpropagate only $k$ steps; bounds memory/compute but ignores longer dependencies.

front: Why vanishing gradients hurt long-range learning
back: The learning signal from the loss to an early input is multiplied by $\approx\rho^{T}$, so early inputs cannot be credited for late errors.
Sequential computation (no parallelism over time), fixed-size memory, hard long-range dependencies.
